library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

```{r model, message = FALSE}
# built once and reused throughout (a 231-state model)
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Ippolito_2024b_pacmilimab_qsp"))
length(mod$state)
```

* Citation: `r mod$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-024-09928-5>
* Supplementary Material 1 (methods, Eqs S1-S18, Figures S1-S3) and
  Supplementary Material 2 (the SimBiology export of the model: Parameters,
  Reactions, Rules, Species and Compartments sheets) of the article

Pacmilimab (CX-072) is a PROBODY therapeutic: an anti-PD-L1 antibody whose two
active sites are each covered by a mask tethered by a protease-cleavable
linker. The mask shifts reversibly to reveal a site (equilibrium constant
`K_m`, the open/closed ratio of one site), and tumour-associated proteases
remove it irreversibly (rate `k_cvg` in the tumour, 1% of that elsewhere). This
paper takes the QSP immuno-oncology platform the Popel laboratory calibrated to
advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC; Wang 2023, npj Precision Oncology),
adds the PROBODY kinetics and out-of-synapse PD-L1 of the authors' earlier
triple-negative breast cancer study (`Ippolito_2024_pacmilimab_qsp`), shifts
the tumour cleavage rate to NSCLC protease activity, and runs a prospective
virtual trial of 10 mg/kg every two weeks for 400 days against the unmasked
antibody.

This is a **deterministic mechanism model**. Virtual patients are drawn by
Latin hypercube sampling of parameter distributions that the paper does not
tabulate, so there are no etas and no residual error, and everything below is a
typical-value simulation at the values of Supplementary Material 2.

# Population

```{r population, echo = FALSE}
pop <- readModelDb("Ippolito_2024b_pacmilimab_qsp")
pop <- eval(body(pop)[[which(vapply(
  as.list(body(pop)),
  function(e) is.call(e) && identical(e[[2]], as.name("population")),
  TRUE
))]][[3]])
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(Field = names(pop), Value = unlist(lapply(pop, as.character))),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

Twenty thousand proposed patients were grown from a single cancer cell; those
whose tumours reached a plausible 3.7 cm pre-treatment diameter were kept, and
a probability of inclusion built from the iAtlas NSCLC distributions of three
bounded immune-subset fractions, `M1/(M1+M2)`, `Treg/(Treg+CD8)` and
`CD4/(CD4+CD8)` (main-text Eqs 1a-1c), selected 460 virtual patients. There is
no clinical trial of pacmilimab in NSCLC; the paper compares its simulated
response rate of about 16% with the 18% reported for unmasked anti-PD-L1
therapy.

# Model structure

| Layer | Content |
|---|---|
| Physiological compartments | central (`V_C`), peripheral (`V_P`), tumour (`V_T`, volume from its cell content), tumour-draining lymph node (`V_LN`) |
| Antigen presentation | APC endosome (`V_e`), endosomal and cell-surface MHC (`A_e`, `A_s`) |
| Synapses | T cell-cancer cell (`syn_T_C1`), T cell-APC (`syn_T_APC`), macrophage-cancer cell (`syn_M_C`) |
| Out-of-synapse | PD-L1 on cancer cells (`nonsyn_C1_T`) and APCs (`nonsyn_APC_LN`) |
| Cells | cancer cells (live and dead), naive and activated CD8 T cells (`T1`), regulatory T cells (`T0`), helper T cells (`Th`), exhausted CD8 and CD4 T cells, APC and mature APC, MDSC, M1 and M2 macrophages |
| Mediators | IL-2, IL-10, IL-12, IFN-gamma, TGF-beta, CCL2, nitric oxide, arginase-I |
| Checkpoints | PD-1/PD-L1/PD-L2, CTLA-4/CD28/CD80/CD86, CD47/SIRP-alpha |
| PROBODY anti-PD-L1 | six free states in each of `V_C`, `V_P`, `V_T`, `V_LN`; nine bound states per PD-L1 pool (cancer cell or APC PD-L1, and T cell PD-L1) in each T-cell synapse |
| Dormant modules | anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA-4 antibodies with the same mask kinetics, never dosed in the paper |

States are integrated as **amounts** (`q_<compartment>_<species>`, in nmol,
molecules or cells) and the declared-unit value is derived as
`x_<compartment>_<species>`, as SimBiology does internally. Cell counts are
molecule counts dimensionally (the platform declares the unit `cell` as
`molecule`), which is what makes the per-cell secretion constants consistent;
the Avogadro constant `NAVG_nmol` bridges nanomole-denominated binding
constants and molecule-denominated surface densities.

The free antibody states are named for the two sites, `c` closed (masked),
`o` open, and a cleaved site dropping its letter:

| Model state | Figure S3 label | Sites |
|---|---|---|
| `aPDL1cc` | cc | both masked (the injected pacmilimab) |
| `aPDL1co` | co | one masked, one open |
| `aPDL1oo` | oo | both open |
| `aPDL1c` | mc | one cleaved, one masked |
| `aPDL1o` | mo | one cleaved, one open |
| `aPDL1` | mm | both cleaved (the unmasked antibody) |

The paper counts as **active** any molecule with at least one site revealed,
whether open or cleaved: every state except `aPDL1cc`.

# Source trace

| Model element | Source (Supplementary Material 2 unless stated) |
|---|---|
| Compartment capacities | Compartments sheet |
| All 225 parameter values, in their original units | Parameters sheet (each `ini()` line quotes the row) |
| Tumour growth, death and dead-cell clearance | Reactions 1-5, 59, 497 |
| Naive and activated CD8, Treg and helper T cells, IL-2 | Reactions 6-57, 443-457 |
| Antigen release, uptake, processing, MHC presentation | Reactions 60-88 |
| Anti-PD-L1 transport, lymphatic drainage, clearance | Reactions 89-124, 161-166 |
| Anti-PD-L1 unmasking and cleavage | Reactions 125-160 |
| Anti-PD-L1 synaptic binding (T cell-cancer cell, T cell-APC, macrophage-cancer cell) | Reactions 311-350, 375-414, 493-494 |
| PD-L1/PD-L2 expression, checkpoint binding | Reactions 351-374, 415-442, 484-496 |
| MDSC, cytokines, macrophages, phagocytosis | Reactions 458-483, 497 |
| Dormant anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA-4 modules | Reactions 167-310, 357-358, 369-370, 421-422, 433-434, 491-492 |
| Tumour volume, totals, Hill terms, T cell generations | Rules sheet, repeated assignments |
| Initial surface densities | Rules sheet, initial assignments |
| Initial cell counts and concentrations | Species sheet |
| Units `cell` = molecule and `mU` = mole/litre | the platform's MATLAB code (`immune_oncology_model_NSCLC.m`, popellab QSPIO), which the export does not state |
| Spherical tumour for RECIST diameters; cleavage outside the tumour at 1% | Supplementary Material 1, "Model implementation" |
| Pre-treatment diameter 3.7 cm; 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks for 400 days | Parameters sheet (`initial_tumour_diameter`); main text, Results |
| Antibody molar mass 145 kDa and body weight 70 kg | not reported; see Assumptions and deviations |

```{r consts}
MW <- 145000 # g/mol (not reported; see Assumptions and deviations)
WT <- 70 # kg (not reported)
nmol_of <- function(mgkg) mgkg * WT / MW * 1e6
dose10 <- nmol_of(10)
SOLVE <- list(atol = 1e-9, rtol = 1e-6, maxsteps = 1e6)
solv <- function(...) {
  do.call(
    rxode2::rxSolve,
    c(list(mod, ...), SOLVE, list(returnType = "data.frame"))
  )
}
FREE <- c("aPDL1cc", "aPDL1co", "aPDL1oo", "aPDL1c", "aPDL1o", "aPDL1")
LABEL <- c(
  aPDL1cc = "cc", aPDL1co = "co", aPDL1oo = "oo",
  aPDL1c = "mc", aPDL1o = "mo", aPDL1 = "mm"
)
ACTIVE <- setdiff(FREE, "aPDL1cc")
TISSUE <- c(V_C = "Serum", V_T = "Tumour", V_P = "Tissue")
q2w <- function(cmt) {
  rxode2::et(amt = dose10, time = 0, cmt = cmt, ii = 14, addl = 28)
}
```

# Initialisation: untreated tumour growth

Each virtual patient is grown from a single cancer cell until the tumour
reaches the pre-treatment diameter, 3.7 cm for NSCLC, and that state starts
the trial.

```{r grow}
grow <- solv(rxode2::et(seq(0, 6000, by = 5)))
i_start <- which(grow$tumour_diameter >= 3.7)[1]
day_start <- grow$time[i_start]
day_start
grow$tumour_diameter[i_start]
inits <- unlist(grow[i_start, mod$state])
names(inits) <- mod$state
```

```{r growfig, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Untreated logistic growth of the typical patient from a single cancer cell to the 3.7 cm pre-treatment diameter."}
ggplot(grow, aes(time, tumour_diameter)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 3.7, linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = day_start, linetype = 3, colour = "grey40") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Day", y = "Tumour diameter (cm)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r reftab, echo = FALSE}
ref <- grow[i_start, ]
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Quantity = c(
      "M1/(M1+M2)", "Treg/(Treg+CD8)", "CD4/(CD4+CD8)", "H_PD1_C1",
      "H_CD28_APC", "H_P1", "H_MDSC"
    ),
    Value = signif(c(
      ref$x_V_T_Mac_M1 / (ref$x_V_T_Mac_M1 + ref$x_V_T_Mac_M2),
      ref$x_V_T_T0 / (ref$x_V_T_T0 + ref$x_V_T_T1),
      (ref$x_V_T_T0 + ref$x_V_T_Th) / (ref$x_V_T_T0 + ref$x_V_T_Th + ref$x_V_T_T1),
      ref$H_PD1_C1, ref$H_CD28_APC, ref$H_P1, ref$H_MDSC
    ), 4)
  ),
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Pre-treatment state of the typical patient: the three selection fractions of Eqs 1a-1c (CD4 taken as Treg plus helper T cells) and the main Hill terms."
)
```

# Structural checks

**Free antibody is conserved.** Unmasking and cleavage only move antibody
between the six free states, and transport only moves it between
compartments; synaptic binding reads the free concentration without consuming
it (the paper's assumption of an abundance of antibody relative to the cell
surface). With both central clearances switched off, the free antibody summed
over the six states and four compartments must therefore stay equal to the
dose. This tests every transport, drainage, unmasking and cleavage term and
the scaling of each by its compartment, including the growing tumour.

```{r masscons}
grid84 <- seq(0, 84, by = 0.5)
ev1 <- rxode2::add.sampling(
  rxode2::et(amt = dose10, time = 0, cmt = "q_V_C_aPDL1cc"), grid84
)
cons <- solv(ev1, inits = inits, params = c(k_cl_aPDL1 = 0, k_cln_aPDL1 = 0))
free_amt <- rowSums(cons[, as.vector(outer(
  c("V_C", "V_P", "V_T", "V_LN"), FREE,
  function(a, b) paste0("q_", a, "_", b)
))])
max(abs(free_amt / dose10 - 1))
stopifnot(max(abs(free_amt / dose10 - 1)) < 1e-4)
```

**The unmasked antibody stays unmasked, and the dormant modules stay at
zero.** Dosing the fully cleaved state must never populate a masked or open
state (cleavage is irreversible), and with neither anti-PD-1 nor anti-CTLA-4
dosed, every one of their states must stay at zero. (The bivalent complexes of
the dormant antibodies pick up integrator round-off of order 1e-13 molecules
during the growth phase, against about 7000 PD-1 molecules per synapse, so
the check allows a 1e-6 tolerance.)

```{r endstate}
ev_um <- rxode2::add.sampling(
  rxode2::et(amt = dose10, time = 0, cmt = "q_V_C_aPDL1"), grid84
)
um <- solv(ev_um, inits = inits)
other_states <- as.vector(outer(
  c("V_C", "V_P", "V_T", "V_LN"), setdiff(FREE, "aPDL1"),
  function(a, b) paste0("q_", a, "_", b)
))
dormant <- grep("aPD1|aCTLA4", mod$state, value = TRUE)
c(
  max_masked_or_open = max(abs(as.matrix(um[, other_states]))),
  max_dormant = max(abs(as.matrix(um[, dormant])))
)
stopifnot(
  max(abs(as.matrix(um[, other_states]))) < 1e-6,
  max(abs(as.matrix(um[, dormant]))) < 1e-6
)
```

# Antibody pharmacokinetics

## Single dose

```{r pk1}
pk1 <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(treatment = "pacmilimab", time = cons$time, Cc = NA_real_),
  data.frame(treatment = "unmasked", time = um$time, Cc = um$Cc)
)
pk1$Cc[pk1$treatment == "pacmilimab"] <- solv(ev1, inits = inits)$Cc
pk1$id <- 1L
```

```{r pk1fig, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Total free antibody in the central compartment (all six states) after a single 10 mg/kg dose of pacmilimab or of the unmasked antibody."}
ggplot(pk1, aes(time, Cc, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Day after dose", y = "Free antibody, central (nmol/L)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r nca}
conc_df <- pk1 |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc))
dose_df <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, treatment = c("pacmilimab", "unmasked"), time = 0, amt = dose10
)
o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment / id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id,
  route = "intravascular", duration = 0
)
ivl <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 84, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE,
  aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE, cl.obs = TRUE
)
res_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = ivl))
```

```{r ncatab, echo = FALSE}
as.data.frame(res_nca) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast", "aucinf.obs", "half.life", "cl.obs")) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Arm = treatment, "Cmax (nmol/L)" = cmax, "AUClast (nmol*day/L)" = auclast,
    "AUCinf (nmol*day/L)" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 (day)" = half.life,
    "CL (L/day)" = cl.obs
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "PKNCA summary of the simulated single-dose profiles (dose 4828 nmol).")
```

The paper publishes no NCA values, so the table documents the model rather
than checking it. Both arms share the atezolizumab-like transport and the
linear clearance of 0.324 L/day; the masked arm clears very slightly faster
because the saturable clearance acts on each antibody state separately (see
below).

## Repeated dosing: Figure S3

Figure S3 of Supplementary Material 1 plots each of the six pacmilimab states
in serum, tumour and peripheral tissue over the 400-day regimen. The serum
bands below were digitised by the maintainers around day 380 of that figure.

```{r s3}
s3 <- solv(rxode2::add.sampling(q2w("q_V_C_aPDL1cc"), seq(0, 400, by = 0.5)),
  inits = inits
)
s3_nocln <- solv(rxode2::add.sampling(q2w("q_V_C_aPDL1cc"), seq(0, 400, by = 0.5)),
  inits = inits, params = c(k_cln_aPDL1 = 0)
)
digitised <- data.frame(
  state = FREE,
  lo = c(850, 8, 0.019, 7.9, 0.047, 0.029),
  hi = c(1900, 20, 0.050, 7.9, 0.047, 0.029)
)
band <- function(s, st) {
  w <- s$time >= 372 & s$time <= 386
  v <- s[[paste0("x_V_C_", st)]][w]
  sqrt(min(v) * max(v))
}
s3tab <- digitised |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    label = LABEL[state],
    fig = sqrt(lo * hi),
    model = vapply(state, function(st) band(s3, st), 1),
    model_nocln = vapply(state, function(st) band(s3_nocln, st), 1),
    ratio = model / fig,
    ratio_nocln = model_nocln / fig
  )
```

```{r s3tab, echo = FALSE}
s3tab |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    State = label,
    "Figure S3 (nmol/L)" = signif(fig, 3),
    "Model (nmol/L)" = signif(model, 3),
    "Model / figure" = signif(ratio, 3),
    "Model, saturable clearance off" = signif(model_nocln, 3),
    "Model / figure, clearance off" = signif(ratio_nocln, 3)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Serum concentration of each pacmilimab state around day 380 of 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks (geometric mid-point of the dosing-interval band).")
```

```{r s3assert}
masked_states <- s3tab$state %in% c("aPDL1cc", "aPDL1co", "aPDL1oo")
stopifnot(
  # the masked and open states, 99% of the drug, match the figure as exported
  all(abs(log(s3tab$ratio[masked_states])) < log(1.5)),
  # all six states match once the saturable clearance is switched off
  all(abs(log(s3tab$ratio_nocln)) < log(1.5)),
  # with it on, the cleaved states sit far below the figure
  all(s3tab$ratio[!masked_states] < 0.2)
)
```

The fully and partly masked states (cc, co, oo) reproduce Figure S3 as
exported, to within 15%. The three states with a cleaved site (mc, mo, mm)
reproduce it only once the saturable clearance `k_cln_aPDL1` is set to zero.
The export applies that clearance (Vmax 5.6 nmol/day, Km 1.69 nmol/L) to each
state separately, so at the low concentrations of the cleaved states it adds
up to 3.3 L/day of clearance, ten times the linear clearance. The figure
behaves as if that term were absent or saturated by total antibody. The model
keeps the exported rate laws and values; set `k_cln_aPDL1 = 0` to reproduce
Figure S3. The choice does not affect tumour response, because the cleaved
states contribute little of the active antibody either way (checked below).

```{r s3fig, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 5.5, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure S3 of Ippolito 2024b for the typical patient: each pacmilimab state in serum (central), tumour and peripheral tissue during 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks."}
s3 |>
  dplyr::select(time, tidyselect::all_of(as.vector(outer(names(TISSUE), FREE, function(a, b) paste0("x_", a, "_", b))))) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "var", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::filter(conc > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cmp = sub("^x_(V_[A-Z]+)_.*$", "\\1", var),
    state = sub("^x_V_[A-Z]+_", "", var),
    tissue = TISSUE[cmp],
    state = factor(LABEL[state], levels = LABEL)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, colour = tissue, linetype = tissue)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~state, nrow = 2) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1e-5, 1e4)) +
  labs(x = "Day of treatment", y = "Concentration (nmol/L)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

Tumour and tissue concentrations sit below the figure's: tumour exposure
depends on the tumour's own size through lymphatic drainage, and the typical
patient's tumour doubles in diameter over the 400 days (below), while the
figure's patient is not identified.

# Virtual trial arms for the typical patient

```{r arms}
grid400 <- seq(0, 400, by = 1)
arms <- list(
  untreated = rxode2::et(grid400),
  pacmilimab = rxode2::add.sampling(q2w("q_V_C_aPDL1cc"), grid400),
  unmasked = rxode2::add.sampling(q2w("q_V_C_aPDL1"), grid400)
)
arm_res <- lapply(names(arms), function(a) {
  s <- solv(arms[[a]], inits = inits)
  s$arm <- a
  s
}) |> bind_rows()
arm_res <- arm_res |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_change = 100 * (tumour_diameter / tumour_diameter[1] - 1)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
```

```{r armfig, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Tumour diameter change from the start of treatment for the typical patient, with the RECIST 1.1 limits of +20% and -30% (compare the spider plot of Figure 3a)."}
ggplot(arm_res, aes(time, pct_change, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(20, -30), linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
  labs(x = "Day of treatment", y = "Tumour diameter change (%)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r armtab, echo = FALSE}
day400 <- arm_res |> dplyr::filter(time == 400)
day400 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Arm = arm,
    "Diameter change at day 400 (%)" = signif(pct_change, 3),
    "PD-1 signalling, T cell-cancer cell (H_PD1_C1)" = signif(H_PD1_C1, 3),
    "PD-1:PD-L1 (molecule/um^2)" = signif(x_syn_T_C1_PD1_PDL1 / 1e10, 3),
    "PD-1:PD-L2 (molecule/um^2)" = signif(x_syn_T_C1_PD1_PDL2 / 1e10, 3)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical patient at day 400. Surface densities are converted from the model's molecule/dm^2.")
```

```{r armassert}
chg <- setNames(day400$pct_change, day400$arm)
pd1pdl1 <- setNames(day400$x_syn_T_C1_PD1_PDL1, day400$arm)
stopifnot(
  # the typical patient progresses in every arm (most virtual patients do)
  all(chg > 20),
  # the unmasked antibody blocks PD-1:PD-L1 by over 95%, pacmilimab by less
  pd1pdl1[["unmasked"]] < 0.05 * pd1pdl1[["untreated"]],
  pd1pdl1[["pacmilimab"]] > pd1pdl1[["unmasked"]]
)
```

The typical patient progresses in all three arms: with an objective response
rate near 16%, most virtual patients do. The unmasked antibody removes over
95% of PD-1:PD-L1 complexes in the T cell-cancer cell synapse, but PD-1
signalling stays high because PD-1:PD-L2 (PD-L2 at 7% of PD-L1, `r_PDL2C1`)
is untouched by an anti-PD-L1 antibody. That leaves PD-L2 as the gate on
response in this patient.

## Responsiveness: a lower PD-L2 patient

To see the two arms separate, the same protocol is run for a patient with
slower tumour growth (`k_C1_growth` 0.003 instead of 0.007 per day) and
little PD-L2 (`r_PDL2C1` 0.001). Both parameters are among the
patient-specific drivers the paper's sensitivity analysis ranks highest
(Figure 4a). This patient is illustrative, not one of the paper's virtual
patients.

```{r responder}
p_resp <- c(k_C1_growth = 0.003, r_PDL2C1 = 0.001)
grow_r <- solv(rxode2::et(seq(0, 10000, by = 5)), params = p_resp)
i_r <- which(grow_r$tumour_diameter >= 3.7)[1]
inits_r <- unlist(grow_r[i_r, mod$state])
names(inits_r) <- mod$state
resp <- lapply(names(arms), function(a) {
  s <- solv(arms[[a]], inits = inits_r, params = p_resp)
  data.frame(arm = a, time = s$time, d = s$tumour_diameter)
}) |> bind_rows() |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_change = 100 * (d / d[1] - 1)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
chg_r <- resp |> dplyr::filter(time == 400)
chg_r <- setNames(chg_r$pct_change, chg_r$arm)
signif(chg_r, 3)
stopifnot(
  # the unmasked antibody shrinks the tumour, and far below the untreated arm
  chg_r[["unmasked"]] < 0,
  chg_r[["untreated"]] - chg_r[["unmasked"]] > 50,
  chg_r[["pacmilimab"]] > chg_r[["unmasked"]],
  chg_r[["pacmilimab"]] <= chg_r[["untreated"]]
)
```

```{r respfig, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "Tumour diameter change for an illustrative low-PD-L2, slow-growing patient."}
ggplot(resp, aes(time, pct_change, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(20, -30), linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
  labs(x = "Day of treatment", y = "Tumour diameter change (%)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

Here the unmasked antibody shrinks the tumour by about a third, at the RECIST
partial-response limit, while pacmilimab barely
slows growth. Pacmilimab's serum exposure matches Figure S3, but only about
1% of it has a site open (`2 * K_m`, with `K_m` = 1/175), and cleavage in the
tumour is slow, so the active antibody in the tumour is roughly fifty-fold
below that of the unmasked arm. The paper reports almost
indistinguishable progression-free survival for the two arms across its 460
virtual patients (Figure 3c). That comparison could not be repeated: the
patient parameter distributions are not in the supplement, and neither
typical-value patient here reproduces the parity.

# Tumour-selective activation

The PROBODY design aims to concentrate active antibody in the tumour. A
volume-free measure of that is the active fraction (active over total free
antibody) in each compartment.

```{r select}
w <- s3$time >= 372 & s3$time <= 386
act_frac <- sapply(c("V_C", "V_P", "V_LN", "V_T"), function(cmp) {
  tot <- rowSums(s3[w, paste0("x_", cmp, "_", FREE)])
  act <- rowSums(s3[w, paste0("x_", cmp, "_", ACTIVE)])
  mean(act / tot)
})
signif(act_frac, 3)
stopifnot(
  act_frac[["V_T"]] > act_frac[["V_C"]],
  act_frac[["V_T"]] > act_frac[["V_P"]]
)
```

The active fraction is highest in the tumour (and in the lymph node it drains
to), about 35% above serum. That is the direction of the paper's selectivity
claim. Figure 3d of the paper plots the cumulative AUC of the percentage of
dose per gram of tissue: about 20 in the tumour, 8 in the central compartment
and 0.06 in the periphery at day 400. Its central value matches **total**
free antibody here (about 10 %dose*day/g with this dose), not the active
antibody, and neither reading reproduces its tumour and periphery curves, so
that panel is not replicated.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Source.** Every equation and value comes from the paper's Supplementary
  Material 2, the SimBiology export of the model the authors ran. Where the
  export and the overview equations of Supplementary Material 1 (Eqs S1-S18)
  differ, the export is encoded, as it is what produced the published
  simulations. The differences are listed below.
* **Units the export does not state.** The platform's MATLAB code defines
  `cell` as `molecule` and `mU` as `mole/litre`. Without the first, every
  per-cell rate is off by Avogadro's number (`k_IFNg_Thsec` = 80.3 "1/day" is
  4e-13/3 nmol per cell per day expressed in molecules per cell per day). Both
  are applied, and a dimensional check then passes for all retained
  reactions and rules with no override.
* **Saturable clearance per state.** As discussed under Figure S3, the
  export's saturable clearance acts on each of the six antibody states
  separately, which suppresses the cleaved states about ten-fold relative to
  the figure. The exported form is kept.
* **Synaptic PD-L1 total.** The repeated-assignment rules for
  `syn_T_C1.PDL1_total` and `syn_T_APC.PDL1_total` sum free PD-L1, PD-1:PD-L1,
  the CD80 complexes and the platform's original single-name antibody
  complexes (`PDL1_aPDL1`, `PDL1_aPDL1_PDL1`), which no reaction forms here.
  They omit the PROBODY-bound states. PD-L1 expression is driven toward
  baseline through these totals, so antibody-bound PD-L1 is replaced by new
  free PD-L1, and since bound complexes have no turnover in the export, they
  accumulate without limit under treatment. This is the exported behaviour
  and is kept. The PD-1 Hill terms read only the PD-1 complexes, so it
  changes no response in this vignette.
* **Out-of-synapse binding.** Supplementary Material 1 describes PROBODY
  binding to PD-L1 outside the synapse (Eqs S16-S18). The export declares the
  bound states but contains no binding reaction for them, so only out-of-synapse
  PD-L1 turnover is active, and the bound states are held at zero. The paper
  states the module has negligible effect, and by construction it cannot
  affect any other state, because binding does not deplete free antibody and
  carries no downstream effect. The T-cell out-of-synapse areas
  (`nonsyn_T_T`, `nonsyn_T_LN`) carry no active species and are omitted.
* **Export details kept as written.** The central-to-lymph-node exchange of
  the doubly open state (reaction 106, and its anti-PD-1 counterpart 182)
  divides the central concentration by `gamma_LN` rather than `gamma_C`. The
  binding of the fully cleaved antibody to T-cell PD-L1 in both synapses
  (reactions 343 and 407) carries a factor of zero. A singly bound
  doubly open complex (`oRo`) is cleaved only at its bound site. Each affects
  a minor state.
* **Never-dosed modules.** The export's anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA-4 antibody
  modules (mask kinetics as for anti-PD-L1, but only the fully cleaved form
  binds) are carried for completeness. Undosed, they are identically zero and
  change nothing else.
* **Parameters dropped.** The 33 rows of the Parameters sheet that are
  targets of repeated-assignment rules (`C_total`, `H_PD1_C1`, `N_aT`, ...)
  hold SimBiology's stored last values. They are computed by their rules
  instead. `A_syn` (the synapse area, carried by the synapse compartment
  capacities) and `k_vas_Msec` (a vasculature constant with no vasculature
  module in this model) appear in no rate law and are omitted.
* **Molar mass and body weight.** Neither is reported: 145 kDa
  (atezolizumab, whose transport parameters the PROBODY shares) and 70 kg are
  assumed to convert 10 mg/kg into 4828 nmol. Both only scale the dose. The
  Figure S3 match of the masked states supports the combination.
* **Virtual population.** The paper's patient-parameter distributions, its
  epsilon bound and the iAtlas selection are not reproducible from the
  supplement, so response rates, progression-free survival, the PRCC analysis
  (Figure 4) and the T cell clone deciles (Figure 5) are not simulated. The
  typical patient and the illustrative low-PD-L2 patient stand in.
* **No IIV, no residual error.** Deterministic mechanism model.
